idea: Audit every crews-plugin consumer that reads envelope summary and catalog where the producer/consumer schema may drift on other fields (kind, replyTo, decision, ack, progressTail, reviewedSeq, bodyResolution). Recommend read-fallback / write-mirror / canonical-type / hybrid.

candidateDirections.name: Runtime schema contract + CI round-trip test (leveraging hooks/protocol/*.js)
candidateDirections.summary: Extend existing hooks/protocol/*.js runtime schema to declare canonical-per-field addresses + one CI round-trip test per producer/consumer pair.

candidateDirections.name: Pick canonical-per-field, delete the mirror, share via envelope module
candidateDirections.summary: Eliminate the dual-address pattern: choose one canonical address per field (payload-nested for system-mailbox, top-level for outbox), delete mirror writes + v1.7.3 read fallback, centralize via hooks/protocol/envelope.js.

candidateDirections.name: Targeted audit ranked by operator-visible failure surface
candidateDirections.summary: Perform the grep-pass deliverable the spawn prompt asked for, but rank findings by operator-visible impact (review-mail render, stop-hook gate, routing lookup) instead of treating all fields symmetrically.

candidateDirections.name: Central consumer normalizer with field-aware read fallbacks
candidateDirections.summary: Extend the v1.7.3 review-mail.js:111 fallback pattern to every consumer via a centralized hooks/protocol/envelope-view.js reader.

candidateDirections.name: Contract-first: write the envelope spec before the audit
candidateDirections.summary: Write docs/envelope-contract.md declaring canonical address per field; any deviation is then by-definition a bug. Audit-or-not, spec ahead of grep survives field additions.

questionsForSynthesis: Is hooks/protocol/*.js schema validation already enforced in CI under CREWS_STRICT_SCHEMA=1? If yes, why did the v1.7.2 summary-drop bug escape it?
Should canonical address be the SAME across appendOutbox and appendSystemMailbox (one global rule) or PER-ENVELOPE-TYPE (outbox top-level, system-mailbox payload-nested)?
Does v1.7.3 keeping BOTH read-fallback AND write-mirror create a third drift source? Should one be reverted in v1.7.4 once the audit picks a winner?
Are row.kind (report kind) and row.from.kind (routing kind) two semantically distinct fields, or one drift candidate?
